displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest affirmative case is a modest cumulative inference: early embodied-resurrection belief and independently traceable institutional and doctrinal continuities make bodily resurrection and Catholic continuity historically credible, although neither conclusion follows from any single source.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the live case by narrowing its conclusion and explicitly making evidential independence and traced continuity necessary.

premises.text: The chronology of undisputed Pauline correspondence makes resurrection belief early, while the distinction between Paul's own experience and inherited witness reports identifies multiple testimonial layers even if it does not guarantee complete independence.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the early-evidence point while incorporating the skeptical limitation concerning secondhand witness material.

premises.text: A bodily reading should rest on contextual criteria such as continuity between burial and resurrection, transformation rather than replacement, and corporate resurrection language, not on the unsupported assertion that no alternative reading exists.

novelty.explanation: This repairs overstatement by supplying explicit interpretive criteria and retaining the visionary objection as a live comparator.

premises.text: Each Pauline, Gospel, patristic, and hostile-witness claim should be assigned a date, information pathway, attested content, and dependence status before its contribution is included in the cumulative case.

novelty.explanation: This directly repairs the missing demonstration of dating, content, informational pathways, and source independence.

premises.text: Continuity should be tested through several invariants, including episcopal structure, sacramental practice, conciliar participation, and central Christological commitments, while allowing regional development and genuine institutional division.

novelty.explanation: This extends the shared-core argument by defining multiple continuity indicators without equating convergence with administrative identity.

conclusion.text: If the embodied reading, source-independence matrix, and continuity invariants survive detailed historical testing, the evidence can make bodily resurrection belief and Catholic continuity credible without claiming that the surviving record compels either conclusion.

novelty.explanation: This repairs disproportionate inference by making the conclusion conditional, cumulative, and expressly short of historical compulsion.

newArguments.title: Dependence-sensitive cumulative confirmation
newArguments.text: A cumulative case need not treat every source as independent or equally reliable. It can discount shared traditions, copying uncertainty, and later preservation while asking whether the residual evidence is still more expected if embodied-resurrection belief arose early than if it emerged only through late legendary development. This framework turns Oppy's objections into explicit evidential discounts instead of ignoring them, and it prevents Albrecht from gaining artificial corroboration merely by counting texts.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a dependence-sensitive comparative framework that neither participant explicitly formulated in the transcript moves.

newArguments.title: Branching rather than linear continuity
newArguments.text: Institutional continuity can be modeled as a branching genealogy rather than a single uninterrupted administrative line. Under that model, Catholic, Orthodox, and Syriac divisions do not erase shared ancestry, but Catholic specificity still requires additional evidence about which structures and practices persist through the Roman branch. This approach incorporates early plurality and later schism without treating every divergence as either total discontinuity or irrelevant variation.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a genealogical model that accommodates both common inheritance and genuine institutional divergence.

thesis.text: The strongest skeptical case is comparative rather than merely negative: the surviving evidence remains substantially expected under visionary experience, inherited interpretation, ordinary textual dependence, selective preservation, and branching institutional development, so it does not securely identify bodily encounters or specifically Catholic continuity.

novelty.explanation: This extends the skeptical route by combining its separate underdetermination mechanisms into one proportionate comparative thesis.

premises.text: Early evidence that Paul believed in resurrection does not by itself establish whether his experience was sensory, visionary, internally generated, or interpreted through traditions he had already received.

novelty.explanation: This extends the distinction between early belief, experience type, and interpretation through inherited reports.

premises.text: Transmission uncertainty should be applied locally: confidence decreases where a claim depends on unidentified sources, late composition, opaque selection, or missing comparators, without assuming that every surviving passage is corrupted.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the overly general application of transmission uncertainty by tying it to identifiable source-level risk factors.

premises.text: Historical conclusions drawn from surviving orthodox and hostile materials should be tested under alternative preservation assumptions, including differential copying, accidental loss, institutional usefulness, and the known survival of some dissenting texts.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the preservation hypothesis by adding competing mechanisms and acknowledging counterevidence from surviving dissenting material.

premises.text: Conciliar definition may formalize an earlier trajectory, but that possibility does not establish that the trajectory was uniquely authoritative, geographically representative, or institutionally identical with later Catholicism.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the conflation of formal definition with prior nonexistence while preserving the challenge to uniquely Catholic identification.

conclusion.text: Unless the affirmative can discriminate bodily encounter from visionary interpretation, demonstrate source-level independence, and trace specifically Catholic institutional continuity through early plurality, historical confidence should remain limited rather than converted into either categorical denial or secure identification.

novelty.explanation: This repairs any excessively negative implication by framing skepticism as proportionate suspension pending three explicit discriminating tests.

newArguments.title: Explicit historical model selection
newArguments.text: The parties can compare rival historical models by listing what each predicts: bodily encounters, sincere visions interpreted through inherited expectation, gradual legendary elaboration, or mixed development. Evidence that every model predicts, such as early sincere belief, has limited discriminatory force. Greater weight should go to evidence that differs across models, including the form of appearance reports, independence of testimonial chains, and whether physical details appear early or accumulate later.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an explicit prediction-based model-selection method absent from the participant moves.

newArguments.title: Counterfactual test for Catholic specificity
newArguments.text: A useful continuity test asks whether the cited evidence would look substantially different if several ancient churches shared apostolic ancestry but later developed competing authority structures. Shared Christology, sacraments, and councils may be expected on that branching hypothesis as well as on specifically Catholic continuity. The affirmative therefore needs Roman-specific, temporally linked evidence that is not equally explained by common inheritance followed by institutional divergence.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a counterfactual specificity test separating common apostolic inheritance from uniquely Catholic continuity.
